name: Terry Taylor
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Terry Taylor owns over 120 car dealerships in the U.S. through his majority stake Automotive Management Services Inc.
Taylor first got into the car business working at his dad's used Ford shop in Daytona Beach, Florida.
Taylor offers his dealership managers equity in his dealerships, usually around 25%.
He owns several high profile properties, including Tommy Hilfiger's former New York penthouse, and a private jet with his initials "TT" on the tail.
forbes_facts: He avoids most meetings, even with his own associates, and only shows up at conventions and conferences on condition that he's not introduced to anyone.

name: Sergei Katsiev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2020)
forbes_bio: Sergei Katsiev, partner of billionaire Igor Kesaev, made his fortune in tobacco after the fall of the Soviet Union.
From 1991 to 1993, he worked in the government trade mission to the Netherlands.
When he returned to Russia, he headed Mercury Tobacco Corporation, an importer of tobacco products owned by Kesaev.
In 1998 Katsiev founded his own company, Megapolis, which also sold tobacco products.
In 2006 Katsiev and Kesaev merged their companies. Megapolis is now Russia's largest seller of tobacco products.
Philip Morris and Japan Tobacco International bought 40% of Megapolis for $1.5 billion in 2013.
forbes_facts: Katsiev is now the owner of Nizhny Karmadon, a mineral water producer sourced from the Caucasus.

name: Pia Hollweg-Vajen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Pia Hollweg-Vajen is a shareholder of Cordes & Graefe, the parent company of the GC Group, a wholesaler that covers a wide range of products for plumbing and HVAC systems.
Founded in 1921 as a pipe and tube trading company, Cordes & Graefe formed the GC Group in 1975 through a series of acquisitions.
Today the company is one of the largest wholesalers in the industry with $17 billion in sales (2023).
Pia Hollweg-Vajen is the daughter of longtime company leader Klaus Hollweg who died in 2023.
forbes_facts: Pia Hollweg-Vajen has an PhD in art studies.

name: Gustavo Cisneros
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (1997-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2023)
forbes_bio: Gustavo Cisneros owns the Cisneros Group, a conglomerate with interests in Venezuelan television, telecom, a brewery, real estate and a baseball team.
In 2007 Cisneros and his partners sold Spanish-language TV network Univision to a group of private equity firms for $12.3 billion (excluding debt).
Cisneros's daughter, Adriana, became CEO in 2013 and restructured the group into 4 branches: media, interactive, real estate and products & services.
In October 2016, Gustavo and wife Patricia gave more than 100 pieces from their Latin American art collection to the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
Cisneros, who is of Cuban heritage, has been a vocal proponent for the normalization of relations between the United States and Cuba.
forbes_facts: In 2000, the Cisneros Group moved its headquarters from Caracas to South Florida.

name: Kwek Leng Peck
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025)
forbes_bio: Kwek Leng Peck is the executive chairman of Singapore-listed Hong Leong Asia, which makes, trades and distributes cement and steel products.
Singapore billionaires Kwek Leng Beng and Kwek Leng Kee are his cousins.
Kwek has a board seat in the family's Hong Leong Finance.
He inherited a stake in Hong Leong Group from his father, Kwek Hong Leong, who cofounded it with the fathers of Kwek Leng Beng and Kwek Leng Kee.
In 2020, Kwek caused a stir by resigning from the board of flagship City Developments, citing differences with the management, such as the company's investments in China.

name: Cargill MacMillan III
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Cargill MacMillan III is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, the world's biggest agriculture business.
His great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.
The Cargill-MacMillan family collects an estimated 18% of net profits as dividends every year.

He owns about a 4% stake in DoorDash, which listed its shares on the New York Stock Exchange in early December 2020.

name: Fan Minhua

forbes_bio: Fan Minhua is the chair and CEO of Hainan Poly Pharm, a pharmaceuticals generics supplier.
Poly Pharm went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2017.

name: Mirwais Azizi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Mirwais Azizi is an Afghan-born real estate developer based in Dubai.
His firm Azizi Developments has delivered more than 45,000 homes since he founded it in 2007 and is currently developing more than 150,000 units in Dubai.
Azizi Developments is building Burj Azizi in Dubai, set to become the second-tallest tower in the world at 2,379 feet.
Azizi fled his native Afghanistan for the Soviet Union in 1989 with just $500. He moved to Dubai in 1994 trading cigarettes, later expanding to oil packaging and exporting and real estate.
Azizi is a major philanthropist in the UAE and Afghanistan, focusing on hospitals, housing and education.

Liang graduated from Guangzhou Medical University in 1988 with undergraduate degree; he received a MBA from National University of Singapore in 2002.

name: Jose Isaac Peres
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Jose Isaac Peres founded Multiplan, a company that develops, owns and manages shopping malls in Brazil.
At age 22 while an economics student, he founded his first company, real estate developer Vepan, which he turned into publicly-traded Multiplan.
He and his wife together own about a quarter of Multiplan's stock.
In 2014 Peres' Village Mall property in Rio de Janeiro became the site of Brazil's first official Apple store.
forbes_facts: Peres, a Rio de Janeiro native, is passionate about his hometown and refuses to move Multiplan's headquarters to Sao Paulo, Brazil's main financial main center.
